approval.restatement: Revision 1.6 as shown: the body is markdown drawn by the Article leaf, and the connected half - two reads, the route and the copy - is built to the same seal.

revisionHistory.change: The reader rebuilt as an executable candidate from the selected direction.
The double tab row extracted to its own block, as the dashboard does it.

Rebuilt from `pages/ContentPage` read line by line: paper card, paywall inside it, footer suppressed when locked, reaction on its own ground, destinations under one name, tab bar never rested, reading column at no seam.
The two rails the plan record puts in this work item: the content map and the on-this-page outline. The entity renamed from `lesson` to `content` across every key, type and fixture field.
The outline entry tinted rather than plated and indented by depth; the map row given its mark, its reading time and its current plate; the module given a summary line that opens and closes.

No pixel changes. The record declares the one environment edit materialization requires: the candidate mirror specifier  becomes . Revision 1.4 was sealed without it, which would have made Apply either write an undeclared difference or stop - and an undeclared edit is exactly what the seal exists to refuse.

The body is markdown, because the data is: `ContentEntity.body` is a markdown column, so `sections` was retired along with `content-article-body` and `heading-over-paragraph`, and two leaves took their place - `Article`, which walks an mdast tree, and `CodeBlock`, whose target folder existed and was empty. The connected half arrived with it: two reads, the route, and the reader's copy in both locales.

candidate.framework: next@16 / react@19 / tailwind@4 / heroui@3, the target's own

mirror.note: contracts/index.ts, contracts/props.ts, branches/Tree, branches/SurfaceCard, branches/SurfaceListCard are the locked target files copied verbatim with their specifiers repointed. Only the contract TABLE is a target write; the rest exist so `ContractKey` closes over the proposed entries.

states.note: The ordinary case: three faces, an article on its paper, the reaction, where to go next, and the pager.
In flight. Title, faces and the whole map are already true; only the article rests.
A content carrying only prose. The face bar is absent rather than drawn with one tab.
Premium. One preview section keeps the paper, the paywall joins it inside, the footer is gone.
The request failed - one notice at the reading measure, no footer, no outline.
First content of a module: the pager stands with no previous.
Last content: the pager stands with no next.
A content that leads nowhere in particular: the joined list is absent rather than titled and empty.

stateCoverage.evidence: The outline rail is absent rather than empty; the same branch runs when a body carries no headings.
Each is its own case with its own states; drawing them from evidence gathered for the reader would settle three surfaces nobody surveyed. Recorded in preview-inventory.md under revision 1.2.

stateCoverage.state: the fade over a locked preview
stateCoverage.evidence: Legacy's `LockedContentMask` is a new owner nobody has approved. The preview is short instead of faded - stated in the page's own header comment and in the revision 1.2 record.

stateCoverage.state: mobile: both rails folded into a bottom bar
stateCoverage.evidence: `LearnMobileTabBar` belongs to `learn-shell-layout`, the case's own work item, and folds rails the shell owns.

stateCoverage.state: every situation the reader can be in
stateCoverage.evidence: The connected half resolves data and renders the pure half; it draws nothing of its own. Its four situations ARE the four states rendered above, reached with fixtures instead of a live server.

stateCoverage.state: which outline entry the reader is level with
stateCoverage.evidence: Scroll-spy needs a live document and an intersection observer. Until it exists no entry claims to be current, because a wrong current entry is worse than none. Recorded as owed rather than done.

relationships.subject: content-reading-column
relationships.reason: The article and the chrome under it are one continuous reading; each block closes with its own trailing space, and legacy's `StackV gap={1}` is a ZERO seam this scale does not name. A rung here would read as the page changing subject.

relationships.subject: content-reading-paper interior
relationships.reason: Legacy's `gap={5}` is 20px and off this ladder. Hint, article and paywall are each already a cluster, which is exactly what the 16px rung names.

relationships.subject: content-reader-footer
relationships.reason: A reaction, where to go next and the content's place in its module each stand alone - block boundaries, not parts of one group.

relationships.subject: content-map-module
relationships.reason: A module's name and the contents under it are one identity, not two facts.

relationships.subject: content-reader-frame
relationships.reason: The layout seam: a rail against the column beside it.

relationships.subject: the content title
relationships.reason: The page is one content; its name is the document's heading and the outline a screen reader builds starts there.

relationships.subject: a module name in the map
relationships.decision: text at sm, not a heading
relationships.reason: The map is a nav, and every module name as a heading would put the whole course tree into the document outline beside the article's own headings.

relationships.subject: the outline entry
relationships.reason: A route is a pill and a tab is an underline because each stands in a bar of peers; an outline entry stands in a column of prose-length lines, where a plate reads as a control rather than as where you are.

relationships.subject: the paywall action
relationships.reason: The paywall is a notice with one way out, which the composite already owns; a second button beside it would offer two.

openQuestions.default: Kept, following `ContentPage` at the reference HEAD.

openQuestions.answeredBy: The reader confirmed after the divergence was stated in conversation (revision 1.4 hand-over).

openQuestions.question: Is the reaction a bare count or a question with a count?
openQuestions.default: A question - `Bài học này hữu ích chứ?` - with the count at the far end.

openQuestions.answeredBy: Accepted at revision 1.2 hand-over without objection after being stated.

openQuestions.question: Are up-next and related content one list or two surfaces?
openQuestions.default: One named joined list - both answer where the reader goes from here.
openQuestions.cost: Loses legacy's distinction between the next content and merely related ones.
openQuestions.answeredBy: Stated as a deliberate merge in preview-inventory.md at revision 1.2; accepted at hand-over.

openQuestions.question: How much of a locked content is shown before the paywall?
openQuestions.cost: A long first section shows more than a short one; the amount is not proportional to the content.
openQuestions.answeredBy: Not raised at hand-over; recorded here so Apply does not treat it as settled by the picture.

openQuestions.question: Syntax highlighting in code blocks
openQuestions.default: None. Mono type on the raised ground, with the fence's language named above it.
openQuestions.cost: A bash block and a TypeScript block look alike; the reference colours both with shiki.
openQuestions.answeredBy: Stated at the 1.6 hand-over as one of three deliberate omissions; not contested.

openQuestions.question: Remark directives (`:::accordion` and friends)
openQuestions.default: Parsed so their markers do not spill into the prose, drawn as ordinary blocks.
openQuestions.cost: Content authored as an accordion reads as a run of paragraphs.
openQuestions.answeredBy: Stated at the 1.6 hand-over; giving directives their own vocabulary is a case of its own.

openQuestions.question: A long command line: wrap or scroll?
openQuestions.cost: Differs from the reference, which scrolls horizontally.
openQuestions.answeredBy: Taken after the first render cut `mongosh "mongodb://...` at the card edge with no closing quote visible.

consolidation.distinguishingFact: Navigation state. A task list has no cursor, so `isCurrent` on `TaskProgressRow` would be a fact that component does not own; a nav link is one line of words rather than a mark, a wrapping title and a trailing reading time; the curriculum line sells a course and carries no progress.

consolidation.reason: NavLink already owns `a destination, marked when it is where you are`, and a place inside the page is a destination. `TextLink.isSelected` draws a choice chip, which is a different statement.
The same double row the dashboard draws; extracted so the reader and the dashboard cannot drift apart.

consolidation.distinguishingFact: Two rails, not one: the flexible column is neither the first nor the last child, which is the whole of what those two entries express.
It opens with the reader's own progress and a filter over the whole tree; the module list is a list of modules and knows nothing about the reader.
Its rows disappear entirely when the module is closed - a disclosure, not a list.
Three children, not two: a name, a count and the control that opens it, and the control must be last so nobody presses the count.
Its entries are depth-bearing places in one document rather than peers; the indent is the content of the relationship.
It declares no seam at all, which is the one thing the page column cannot express.
It caps the READING measure rather than a panel width, and admits a paywall as a sibling of the body it is hiding.
Every child is independently capped to the reading measure; the page column caps once, at the top.
The reaction answers the whole content rather than a sentence above it, so the prompt sits BESIDE it on one row rather than over it.
Its rows carry no completion mark: a tick would promise something to finish, and these are places to open.
It ends in a disclosure glyph rather than a fact - the row leads somewhere.
It is prose sections inside a surface that already owns the measure, so it caps nothing itself.

It draws INLINE structure - a bold phrase, a piece of code inside a sentence, a link mid-clause. Every text leaf in this house takes `content: string`, which holds a sentence but not a sentence with a link inside it.
A passage the reader will run rather than read: it keeps its own whitespace, names its language, and never re-flows into prose measure.
Its answer is PERSONAL to the viewer for the same id - the server truncates a premium body per entitlement - so the viewer is in the key for correctness rather than for hygiene.
It outlives a page turn: the content it maps is replaced while the map stays true, which is the whole reason it is a second read.
Authenticated rather than optional-auth: the server refuses an anonymous read of a content.
Login-only rather than enrolment-gated - a trial reader may see a module's shape without opening its premium contents.

integrationEdits.reason: Mirror specifier repoint only. During Preview the candidate imports its contract machinery and its own not-yet-landed files through `~candidate/*`, because `ContractKey` closes over the table ON DISK and these files do not exist in the target yet. Once they land the mirror has no reason to exist, so every `~candidate/` specifier becomes `@/` and nothing else changes. The edit is mechanical, total and checkable: no `~candidate` may remain in a materialized file.

Merged rather than copied. `src/messages/<locale>.json` already carries every other surface's copy, so materialization adds the `learn` key to the existing object instead of replacing the file. The candidate file IS that merge computed against the target at seal time, which is why it is byte-for-byte what should land - but a target that gained other strings meanwhile must be re-merged rather than overwritten.
